extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) preparing ex parte appeal briefs, reply briefs, or requests for rehearing before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical tips for drafting effective ex parte appeal briefs, reply briefs, and requests for rehearing to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, including what to include, what to avoid, and procedural scope. Focus is on persuading the Board and complying with PTAB practice (37 C.F.R. §§ 41.37, 41.41, 41.52).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present only the strongest arguments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dilute strong arguments by including weaker arguments or arguments that have no bearing on the issues in the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategically group and organize claim arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategically group claims to highlight the strongest arguments in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give careful thought to which claims you choose to argue separately so that weaker arguments do not dilute stronger arguments. For those claims argued separately, place such arguments under separate sub-headings. If the same arguments are being made for patentability of two or more independent claims, argue these claims as a group under a single heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop factual record and apply the legal standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop the facts of your case to show how the law applies to achieve the result being sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out the standard for the legal theory you seek to have applied, and then provide arguments or evidence to demonstrate the legal theory applies to the case before the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the examiner's rejection and identify error
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly address the examiner's rejection as articulated in the rejection on appeal and point the Board to the alleged error in that rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct the Board to the specific error(s) in the examiner's reasoning as written in the rejection on appeal; tie your arguments to the actual rejection text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and address burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when the burden of proof shifts to appellant and provide arguments to show why the burden should not be shifted or provide evidence to rebut the examiner's findings and meet the burden of proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define key claim terms and argue claim construction under BRI
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge when an issue turns on claim construction and provide an interpretation for the key claim terms with a basis for the interpretation under the 'broadest reasonable interpretation' standard. Demonstrate why the examiner's interpretation is not 'reasonable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Support arguments with evidence; do not substitute attorney argument
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney argument cannot substitute for evidence. Do not rely on new evidence that was not before the examiner during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish appealable issues from petitionable matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the difference between appealable and petitionable issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board reviews adverse decisions of examiners (i.e., claim rejections). The Board typically does not review matters within the examiner's discretion (i.e., objections to the figures or specification, restriction requirements, refusal to enter an amendment, etc.). These matters are decided by the Director on petition. See MPEP § 1002.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Summary of Claimed Subject Matter effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Summary of Claimed Subject Matter to support your appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board uses the Summary of Claimed Subject Matter portion of the appeal brief to understand the claimed invention and how the claim elements correspond to the drawing elements and the description in the specification. This section is particularly important when the claim recites elements in §112(f) (means-plus-function) format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit reply briefs to responding to Examiner's Answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Use reply briefs to respond to points raised in the Examiner's Answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reiterate arguments presented in the appeal brief. Use the reply brief to reply to specific findings made, or positions taken, by the examiner in the answer, or to address intervening case law relevant to the issues on appeal. Do not raise new arguments in a reply brief that are not responsive to arguments made in the examiner's answer. Do not separately argue claims for the first time in a reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: File requests for rehearing only when appropriate and narrowly focused
rubrics_metrics.description: File requests for rehearing only when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not simply re-argue the points raised in the briefs. Identify particular points of error by the Board. Strategically limit arguments to only one or two assertions of error, and refer to the specific portions of the Board's opinion where the errors can be found.
